automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.policy: Only sources published or visibly updated after the start and at or before the run timestamp qualify; date-only cutoff-day candidates are excluded unless after-cutoff time is visible.

selection_policy: New or unchecked leaves first, then oldest last_checked_at, ties by stable relative path sort; index, digest, maintenance, federation, schema, glossary, known-defects, open-decisions, topic-index, and non-durable dated synthesis pages excluded.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: arXiv paper frames agent context management as a lifecycle spanning deciding what to remember, extraction, store choice, scoped retrieval, anticipation, compaction, consolidation, forgetting stale information, and provenance; it argues naive accumulation grows token cost quadratically and benchmark claims need methodology separation.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Reinforces context-state externalization and rehydration as lifecycle architecture rather than a generic memory store, and supports keeping compaction, provenance, and cost behavior explicit in local context guidance.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: During ingest, route vendor and benchmark background upstream; keep the local practice implication about lifecycle-managed context, provenance, and cost-aware compaction.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: eGain describes AI agent response governance as a knowledge-governance layer: current, relevant, unambiguous source material; prioritization by question frequency, value, and complexity; consolidation into a governed source of truth; contradiction resolution; taxonomy; and ongoing drift controls.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Supports local raw-intake and automated-feed practice: source freshness, contradiction handling, taxonomy, and human review are part of keeping agent-facing wiki or knowledge content safe to retrieve.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Preserve only the local knowledge-governance workflow implication; route product/vendor background upstream.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar opinion piece argues AI agents should be discoverable first-class identities with lifecycle governance, designated human owners, clear policies, audit trails, and just-in-time privileged access rather than direct exposure to long-lived secrets.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Strengthens the local approval-boundary and ownership-roster rule that autonomous agents need named human ownership, scoped permissions, auditable access, and secret-minimizing controls.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Keep identity-provider background upstream; local ingest should focus on owner, policy, audit, and just-in-time access implications.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar opinion piece warns that autonomous AI agents can create spend and accountability sprawl because usage scales continuously across external services; it recommends early visibility, cost-to-outcome mapping, infrastructure-level controls, and ownership from deployment day one.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Adds a current cost-governance angle for hybrid infrastructure economics and adoption agreements: budget ownership, consumption review, and control placement must be explicit before agent deployments scale.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Route broad regulatory and vendor context upstream; retain local cost-owner and infrastructure-control implications.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar opinion piece argues AI overload comes from weak system design, not usage itself: many employees still orchestrate prompts, validation, and corrections manually, while structured multi-agent workflows and adaptive operating models should place human judgment at the right control points.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Supports local operating agreements and approval boundaries by separating strategic human review from constant manual supervision, and treating architecture as the lever for reducing orchestration burden.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Keep jurisdiction-specific employment-law details upstream or governance-owned; local page should focus on right-sized human review and workflow architecture.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Business Insider reports that AI coding tools are reshaping daily engineering workflows, changing expectations for coding jobs, and raising an unresolved junior-talent problem because senior engineers often benefit most from AI while entry-level debugging and simple-feature work may be automated.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Qualifies for the junior-learning leaf because it reinforces that apprenticeship paths must intentionally preserve debugging, review, and technical-judgment practice as agents absorb simpler work.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Use only the local talent-pipeline implication; route broad publication, company, and labor-market background upstream.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: AakashX argues AI adoption is an operating-model change with workflow ownership, data readiness, architecture, governance, human oversight, operations after go-live, cost tracking by workflow, and review cadence; it warns against measuring usage instead of useful outcomes.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Directly supports adoption operating agreements, ownership rosters, automated update/feed governance, and raw monitor follow-up rules by tying AI systems to owners, source freshness, runbooks, approval gates, logs, cost, and monthly review.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: If ingested, keep vendor identity upstream and focus locally on ownership, freshness, cost-per-outcome, approval, logs, and operating review cadence.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Sponsored Business Insider/Dell piece says agentic workflows multiply token use and positions local/deskside agent execution as a way to control token cost, keep sensitive work local, enforce policies, and maintain logs before scaling to larger infrastructure.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Adds a current infrastructure-economics candidate for balancing managed APIs, local execution, cost telemetry, privacy, and governance controls.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Treat as sponsored/vendor-positioned evidence; route product background upstream and keep only local cost/privacy/governance design implications.
